evidence.quote: Of course, because monetary policy affects the economy with a lag, we should not wait until we have reached our objectives to begin adjusting policy.
Once we begin to remove policy accommodation, the Committee's assessment is that economic conditions will likely warrant raising the federal funds rate only gradually.
Turning to price stability, the other goal of our dual mandate, we have seen little progress toward inflation moving back to our target of 2 percent.
In addition, U.S. labor markets have continued to improve.
It goes without saying that we are also mindful of the risks of tightening policy prematurely.

parsed.rationale: The speech restates FOMC guidance pointing toward an eventual liftoff while stressing gradualism, below-target inflation and the risks of premature tightening. These hawkish and dovish elements roughly balance, leaving a near-neutral stance with a slight tilt toward normalization.
